tasks.short: Lead team meetings and assign work, supervise staff on cases, track team tasks and deadlines, and approve leave and hours.

steps.what: Public health physician coordinates the work of physicians, nurses and statisticians in team meetings
Public health physician supervises staff members on cases
Staff update their tasks and deadlines on the shared project board
Public health physician tracks team tasks and deadlines: in a spreadsheet today, on the shared project board after the change
Public health physician reads leave and hours requests: by e-mail today, as workflow items with the team's planned absence shown after the change
Public health physician checks each request: dates or hours against the team's planned absence and agreed hours
Public health physician approves the checked request in the HR system

tasks.design: Team tasks and deadlines sit on a shared project board ({PROJECT}) that staff update themselves, so the physician does not keep a spreadsheet. Leave and hours arrive as workflow items in the HR system ({HCM}) with the team's planned absence shown; the physician checks each request and approves it once. Leading meetings and supervising cases stay with the physician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tasks were tracked in a spreadsheet and requests handled by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Project boards and HR workflows are standard.
tasks.human_edge: Supporting a nurse after a hard case.

evidence.claim: Project boards and HR request workflows are standard tools.
Systems that track staff tasks can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from team work to requests decided; hiring is outside.
Input contract: staff update the board; fallback is the spreadsheet.

Staff update tasks on the board (s3u) in about the time e-mail updates took; their time is outside the physician's savings. s3 keeps 50 for reading the board and following up late tasks; s4 keeps 50 for reading requests; the check and the approval keep their full time.

incremental.description: Public health physician keeps the board's structure current.

approvals.approved_version: The leave or hours request with its dates and hours exactly as checked by the physician in s4c, approved once in the HR system for that staff member; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: staff rarely update the board, so the spreadsheet partly stays (s3 keeps 80), and requests still come by e-mail (s4 keeps 80) (3.9); high: staff use the board and the HR workflow (10.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect notifications and lab reports, combine data and compute rates, review flagged signals and decide on action, and write the weekly surveillance report.

steps.what: Public health physician collects notifiable disease reports and lab reports
Public health physician uses surveillance data to compute rates in spreadsheets
Public health physician reviews signals to identify health risks and decides on action
Public health physician writes the weekly surveillance report
Public health physician checks the final report: figures against the dashboard, the assessment against the signals reviewed, and the distribution list
Public health physician publishes the checked weekly report to the agreed distribution list

tasks.design: Laboratory and physician notifications arrive electronically in the surveillance system ({DATA_PLATFORM}) instead of by e-mail and fax. A scripted pipeline computes case counts, rates per age group and area, and compares them with set thresholds, flagging signals on a dashboard ({BI}). The weekly report template fills tables and charts, and the physician writes the assessment, checks the final report and publishes it once. Reviewing signals and deciding on action stay with the physician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were collected from mailboxes and rates computed in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Surveillance systems take electronic notifications; scripts compute rates and thresholds.
tasks.still_hard: Some notifications still arrive by phone.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a cluster that the threshold does not flag.
tasks.altitude: The physician assesses signals instead of compiling data.

evidence.claim: Surveillance systems can take electronic notifications and compute rates against thresholds.
Health data are special category data; processing for public health needs a legal basis and a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from new reports to the report written; outbreak control is outside.
Input contract: labs notify electronically; fallback is mailboxes.

Reviewing signals, deciding on action and the report check keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 for reports that still arrive by mail; s2 keeps 30 for checking the pipeline output; s4 keeps 60 because tables and charts fill and the physician writes the assessment.
Thresholds are set and reviewed by the team.

incremental.description: Public health physician reviews thresholds each season.

approvals.approved_version: The weekly surveillance report exactly as checked by the physician in s4c, published once to the agreed distribution list for that week; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many notifications still come by phone and mail (s1 keeps 70) and the template fills few tables (s4 keeps 80) (26.6); high: mostly electronic notifications (36.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide program topics and targets with partners, direct staff who deliver education, review campaign materials, track reach and participation, and report progress.

steps.what: Public health physician directs public health education programs by deciding topics and targets with partners
Public health physician directs staff who deliver education on immunizations and preventable diseases
Public health physician reviews campaign materials for medical accuracy
Staff register sessions held and attendance in the registration system
Public health physician tracks reach and participation in spreadsheets
Public health physician writes the progress report for the board
Public health physician checks the final progress report: figures against the dashboard and the assessment, for the board
Public health physician sends the checked progress report to the board

tasks.design: A dashboard ({BI}) shows sessions held, people reached, sign-ups and vaccination uptake per program and area, fed from the registration and vaccination systems, so reach is not tallied in spreadsheets. The progress report template fills those figures, and the physician writes the assessment, checks the report and sends it once to the board. Staff register sessions and attendance in the registration system. Setting topics, directing staff and reviewing materials stay with the physician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reach was tallied in spreadsheets and reports built by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Dashboards read registration and vaccination systems.
tasks.still_hard: Partners' activities are not in the systems.
tasks.human_edge: Convincing a hesitant community to trust vaccination.

evidence.claim: Dashboards can read registration and vaccination systems to show reach per area.
Health data are special category data; dashboards use aggregated figures.

assumptions: Boundary: from health priorities to progress reported; funding is outside.
Input contract: programs registered in the system; fallback is spreadsheets.

Directing programs, reviewing materials and the report check keep their full time. s4 keeps 40 for reading the dashboard and partner figures; s5 keeps 70 because the template fills figures and the physician writes the assessment. Staff registration (s4r) is outside the physician's savings.

incremental.description: Public health physician adds partner activity figures by hand.

approvals.approved_version: The progress report exactly as checked by the physician in s5c, sent once to the board for that period; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many programs are not registered, so spreadsheets partly stay (s4 keeps 70) and the report fills little (s5 keeps 85) (4.9); high: programs registered as designed (10.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define evaluation questions and measures, collect outcome data, analyse it, interpret the results, and write the evaluation report.

steps.what: Public health physician defines evaluation questions and measures
Public health physician collects outcome data from registries and surveys
Public health physician analyses data to evaluate the effectiveness of risk reduction measures
Public health physician interprets the results
Public health physician writes the evaluation report
Public health physician checks the final evaluation report: tables against the script output, conclusions against the results and their limits, and the policy makers it goes to
Public health physician sends the checked evaluation report to the policy makers

tasks.design: A versioned analysis script reads the registries and survey data into one pseudonymised store ({DATA_PLATFORM}) and computes the agreed measures before and after the intervention, so data are not collected and analysed by hand each time. The report template fills tables and charts from the script's output, and the physician writes the conclusions, checks the report and sends it once to the policy makers. Defining the evaluation and interpreting results stay with the physician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were collected from several registries and analysed in spreadsheets each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned scripts and pseudonymised data stores are standard in public health.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a drop in cases came from the measure or from chance.
tasks.altitude: The physician interprets instead of compiling.

evidence.claim: Versioned analysis scripts can read registries and compute agreed measures.
Health data are special category data; secondary use needs safeguards and a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from the intervention running to the report written; policy decisions are outside.
Input contract: data access agreed with registries; fallback is manual extracts.

Defining, interpreting and the report check keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 for data the script cannot read; s3 keeps 50 for checking the script output; s5 keeps 70 because tables and charts fill and the physician writes the conclusions.
Policy makers' time does not change.

incremental.description: Public health physician maintains the analysis script.

approvals.approved_version: The evaluation report exactly as checked by the physician in s5c, sent once to the named policy makers; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off evaluations with new measures, so much data is still extracted and analysed by hand (s2 keeps 70, s3 keeps 80) (15.4); high: repeated evaluations with set measures (31.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The public health physician keeps supervising staff, assessing signals, directing programs and interpreting evaluations; spreadsheets, mailbox collection and hand-built reports shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A physician with more time for public health action.
